mainTopic: Working on תשעה באב and on ערב פסח: יוהרא, custom versus prohibition, and finishing versus starting work
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier question: the תנא listed only the leniencies of תשעה באב. The גמרא then asks why רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the רבנן seem to switch positions on יוהרא (showing off) between our משנה and the משנה about a חתן reading קריאת שמע. רבי יוחנן switches the names in one source. רב שישא keeps both texts and explains why each side is consistent. Next comes a new משנה about working on ערב פסח in יהודה and the גליל, and about the night before. The גמרא asks why one משנה calls it a custom and this one a prohibition. רבי יוחנן answers that the two משניות follow רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. A ברייתא about replanting a stalk on the 13th raises a question on רבי יהודה, and רבא, רב ששת, רב אשי and רבינא each answer it. Finally, a new משנה gives רבי מאיר's rule that work begun before the 14th may be finished on it. The גמרא asks whether this applies to festival work, non-festival work, or both. A first proof from a small belt and hairnet is pushed off, and a second proof from רבי מאיר begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The תנא only listed leniencies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the previous discussion: the תנא only listed the ways תשעה באב is more lenient than a public fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא is teaching only leniencies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final answer to a question from the previous section. The question was why the משנה left out the ways תשעה באב is stricter than a public fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה was never meant to list every difference between תשעה באב and a public fast. It only lists the leniencies. So leaving out the stringencies is not a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of the משנה or ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: The list in the משנה is a list of leniencies only. It is not a complete list of differences.

phrases.english: The Tanna is teaching a list of leniencies.
phrases.notes: Doubling a word ('leniencies, leniencies') means 'one leniency after another,' a whole series of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a question earlier about why the משנה is incomplete.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the scope of the list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה should have listed every difference, including stringencies.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only meant to list leniencies.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about Torah scholars
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes our משנה: everywhere, תלמידי חכמים do not work on תשעה באב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And in all places Torah scholars [are idle]', and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה to start a new discussion. This is a setup line for the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full משנה says that תלמידי חכמים are idle on תשעה באב everywhere. It adds that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says a person should always make himself like a תלמיד חכם. The implication is that the רבנן do not let an ordinary person stop working. Only רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.: the quote continues in the source

phrases.english: 'And in all places Torah scholars [are idle],' etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says a person should always act like a תלמיד חכם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תלמידי חכמים refrain from work on תשעה באב. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל lets anyone act like a תלמיד חכם.

steps.title: What does each side hold about showing off?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the משנה: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is not worried about יוהרא, but the רבנן are.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds we are not worried about showing off, and the רבנן hold we are worried about showing off?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the reasoning behind each opinion in the משנה. This prepares the contradiction that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would the רבנן stop an ordinary person from not working? Because it looks like he is pretending to be a scholar. That is יוהרא. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows it, so it seems he is not bothered by that concern.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (introduces a conclusion the גמרא will question)
Arrogance, showing off as more pious than others

phrases.aramaic: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סָבַר:
phrases.english: Is that to say that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds:
we are not concerned about showing off,
and the Rabbis hold: we are concerned about showing off?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the reasoning behind the משנה quoted in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the dispute in the משנה really about whether we worry about יוהרא?

steps.title: Contradiction from the groom reading שמע
steps.stepSummary: In a משנה in ברכות, the opinions are reversed. The רבנן let a חתן read שמע. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל forbids it because of יוהרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we heard them say the opposite! As the משנה teaches: a groom who wants to read קריאת שמע on the first night may read. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: not everyone who wants to take the name [of a pious person] may take it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading from the last step. It quotes another משנה where each side seems to hold the opposite view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חתן is exempt from שמע on his wedding night. In ברכות, the רבנן let him read it anyway, so they are not worried about יוהרא. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל objects because it looks like showing off. So each side contradicts what it said in our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
To take on the reputation (of being pious)

steps.confusionAlert: The contradiction works in both directions. The רבנן contradict the רבנן, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל contradicts רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. Keep both in mind, because the answers deal with each side separately.

phrases.english: But we heard them say the opposite, as we learned:
A groom, if he wishes to read
Shema on the first night, he may read.
phrases.notes: This is the view of the רבנן (תנא קמא).

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא כׇּל הָרוֹצֶה לִיטּוֹל אֶת הַשֵּׁם יִטּוֹל.
phrases.english: Not everyone who wishes to take the name may take it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of step 3 with a contradicting משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The views about יוהרא given to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the רבנן in step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In ברכות, the רבנן ignore יוהרא and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל worries about it. That is the reverse of our משנה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the names are switched
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the names in one of the sources should be switched.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: the opinions are reversed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the contradiction by fixing the text. One of the two משניות has the names swapped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the names are switched in one source, each תנא holds the same view in both places. This answer changes the text itself. It does not explain why the cases are different.

keyTerms.meaning: The line of opinions (who said what)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: the opinions are reversed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות are accurate as written, so the views contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: One משנה has the names swapped, so there is no real contradiction.

steps.title: רב שישא: the רבנן are consistent
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא keeps the text as it is. Not working while everyone else works stands out as showing off. Reading שמע when everyone else reads it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא son of רב אידי said: do not reverse. The רבנן against the רבנן is not a problem. Here, since everyone works and he does not, it looks like showing off. But there, since everyone reads [שמע] and he also reads, it does not look like showing off.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא offers a different answer. He does not change the text. He first explains why the רבנן are consistent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן do worry about יוהרא, but only when a person's behavior stands out. On תשעה באב, everyone is working, so one person sitting idle is noticed. With שמע, everyone is reading it, so the חתן blends in.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that יוהרא depends on how an act looks to others. Not every extra act of piety is showing off. Only one that makes a person stand out is.

phrases.aramaic: רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi said:
Do not reverse:
The Rabbis against the Rabbis is not difficult;

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא, כֵּיוָן דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא עָבְדִי מְלָאכָה
phrases.english: here, since everyone is doing work
and he is not working, it looks like showing off,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָתָם, כֵּיוָן דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא קָרֵי
phrases.english: but there, since everyone is reading [Shema]

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיהוּ נָמֵי קָרֵי — לָא מִיחְזֵי כְּיוּהֲרָא.
phrases.english: and he is also reading, it does not look like showing off.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר לָא תֵּיפוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the text change of step 5 and gives another way to answer the contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (based on how the act looks to others)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן were inconsistent about יוהרא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן worry about יוהרא only when the act makes a person stand out.

steps.title: רב שישא: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is consistent
steps.stepSummary: With שמע, everyone knows a חתן cannot concentrate, so reading it is showing off. Not working on תשעה באב is not, because people assume he just has no work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל against רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is not a problem. There, we need concentration, and we all know he cannot concentrate, so it looks like showing off. But here it does not look like showing off. People say: he just has no work. Go out and see how many idle people are in the market.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא finishes his answer. He now explains why רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is also consistent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קריאת שמע requires כוונה, and a חתן is clearly too distracted to have it. So when he reads, he is claiming a focus nobody believes he has, and that is יוהרא. Sitting idle on תשעה באב claims nothing, because plenty of people are unemployed anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: We are witnesses: it is obvious to everyone

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree that יוהרא matters. They disagree about which act looks like showing off. The רבנן ask whether the act stands out from what others are doing. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל asks whether the act claims something people know isn't true.
steps.confusionAlert: רב שישא's two halves use different reasons. For the רבנן, the reason is whether the act stands out. For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the reason is whether the act claims a piety or focus people know is false. Do not mix them up.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel

phrases.aramaic: אַדְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לָא קַשְׁיָא;
phrases.english: against Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is not difficult;
there it is that we require concentration,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲנַן סָהֲדֵי דְּלָא מָצֵי כַּוּוֹנֵי דַּעְתֵּיהּ —
phrases.english: and we are witnesses that he cannot focus his mind,
so it looks like showing off;
but here it does not look like showing off,
people say: it is work that he does not have,

phrases.aramaic: פּוֹק חֲזִי כַּמָּה בַּטְלָנֵי אִיכָּא בְּשׁוּקָא.
phrases.english: go out and see how many idle people there are in the marketplace.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אַדְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of רב שישא's answer. Step 6 handled the רבנן; this handles רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (what the act claims)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was inconsistent about יוהרא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל worries about יוהרא only when the act claims a piety or focus people know is not there. Being idle claims nothing.

steps.title: The new משנה: יהודה, the גליל, and the night before פסח
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say that in יהודה people worked on ערב פסח until חצות, and in the גליל they did not work at all. About the night before, בית שמאי forbid work and בית הלל allow it until sunrise.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: חכמים say: In יהודה, people did work on the day before פסח until midday. In the גליל, they did not work at all. About the night before: בית שמאי forbid work, and בית הלל allow it until sunrise.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a new משנה. It tells us how work on ערב פסח was handled in two regions. It also tells us what בית שמאי and בית הלל say about the night of the fourteenth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part is told as a report about what people in each region did. The second part uses legal words: אוסרים (forbid) and מתירין (permit). Those strong words are what the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: The days before Pesach (the 14th of ניסן)

steps.confusionAlert: The night in the בית שמאי and בית הלל argument is the night that begins the 14th. It is the night before ערב פסח day, not the night of the סדר.

phrases.english: MISHNA: And the Rabbis say:
In Judea they would do work
on the days before Pesach until midday,

phrases.aramaic: וּבַגָּלִיל לֹא הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין כׇּל עִיקָּר.
phrases.english: and in the Galilee they would not work at all.
The night: Beit Shammai forbid,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַתִּירִין עַד הָנֵץ הַחַמָּה.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel permit until sunrise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins after the discussion of יוהרא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Judea worked until midday, and the Galilee did not work at all. On the night before, בית שמאי forbid work and בית הלל permit it until sunrise.

steps.title: Custom at first, prohibition at the end?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a contradiction. The earlier משנה treated not working on ערב פסח as a custom, but this משנה speaks of it as a prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: At first the תנא taught that it is a custom. At the end, he taught that it is a prohibition!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. The earlier משנה said not working depends on local custom. Here, with words like אוסרים, it sounds like actual forbidden law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If it is only a custom, each place should follow its own practice. Forbidding work outright treats it as an איסור. One תנא cannot hold both views, so the two מִשְׁנָיוֹת seem to contradict each other.

phrases.english: GEMARA: At first, he taught custom,
phrases.notes: The earlier משנה: 'a place where they were accustomed'

phrases.english: and at the end, he taught prohibition!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעִיקָּרָא תְּנָא מִנְהָגָא, וּלְבַסּוֹף תְּנָא אִיסּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of the earlier משנה (custom) and this משנה (prohibition)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same activity cannot be only a custom and also an actual prohibition in one consistent teaching.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: two different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the earlier משנה follows רבי מאיר and this משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: It is not a difficulty. That one follows רבי מאיר, and this one follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the contradiction. He says each משנה follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'custom' משנה follows רבי מאיר. The 'prohibition' משנה follows רבי יהודה. Since two people hold two views, there is no contradiction.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: It is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: הָא — רַבִּי מֵאִיר, הָא — רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: That one is Rabbi Meir, this one is Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the two sources to different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both מִשְׁנָיוֹת were thought to reflect one view.
steps.terutzMaskana: The custom משנה follows רבי מאיר, and the prohibition משנה follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר argue
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the מחלוקת. רבי יהודה describes Judea and the Galilee. רבי מאיר replies that it depends only on local custom.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי יהודה said: In יהודה they worked on the day before פסח until midday, and in the גליל they did not work at all. רבי מאיר said to him: What do יהודה and the גליל have to do with this? Rather, where people are used to working, they work. Where they are used to not working, they do not work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רבי יוחנן. In it, רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר argue about this exact issue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה ties the rule to regions, which sounds like a fixed law. רבי מאיר rejects the regions and makes it depend on what each place is used to. That is the language of custom.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
What does this have to do with here?
A place where they were accustomed

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda said:
In Judea they would do work
on the days before Pesach until midday,
and in the Galilee they do not work at all.
Rabbi Meir said to him:
What do Judea and the Galilee have to do with here?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלָאכָה — עוֹשִׂין,
phrases.english: Rather, a place where they were accustomed to do work, they work;

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ שֶׁלֹּא לַעֲשׂוֹת — אֵין עוֹשִׂין.
phrases.english: a place where they were accustomed not to work, they do not work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree about custom versus prohibition
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the exchange between רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר

steps.title: Inference: רבי יהודה means a real prohibition
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי מאיר is talking about custom, רבי יהודה must be talking about a prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since רבי מאיר speaks about custom, we can infer that רבי יהודה is speaking about a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the point out of the ברייתא. רבי מאיר's reply shows that רבי יהודה must have meant an איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר argues with רבי יהודה by saying it is only custom. So רבי יהודה must hold the opposite: in the גליל, working is truly forbidden. This completes the proof for רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, the earlier 'custom' משנה follows רבי מאיר. This 'prohibition' משנה follows רבי יהודה, who treats not working in the גליל as an איסור.

phrases.english: Since Rabbi Meir says custom,
it follows that Rabbi Yehuda is saying prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר מִנְהָגָא מִכְּלָל דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אִיסּוּרָא קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה holds that not working is an איסור, and רבי מאיר holds it is a מנהג.

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה really allow work on the fourteenth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה truly allows work on the 14th in יהודה. It quotes a ברייתא where he rules about replanting a stalk pulled up while weeding on the 13th.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה hold that work is permitted on the fourteenth? But it was taught: רבי יהודה says: One who is weeding on the thirteenth, and a stalk was uprooted in his hand, may replant it in a muddy place, but may not replant it in a dry place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge against רבי יהודה. It quotes a ברייתא that mentions only the 13th, as if work on the 14th were not an option. The גמרא is setting up a contradiction; the full point is spelled out next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, Judea may work until midday on the 14th. Yet his ruling about replanting is set on the 13th. This hints that on the 14th one could not do this work at all, even in Judea. In mud the stalk takes root quickly, before the עומר on the 16th, so it becomes permitted. In dry ground it would root only later, so it stays forbidden until the next year's עומר.

keyTerms.meaning: It was uprooted in his hand
But it was taught (introduces a contradicting ברייתא)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never says anything is forbidden on the 14th. The challenge comes from the fact that it mentions only the 13th, as if that were the last day for this work.

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yehuda hold that the fourteenth
is permitted for doing work?
But it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One who weeds on the thirteenth, and a stalk was uprooted in his hand,
replants it in a muddy place,
phrases.notes: It roots quickly, before the עומר on the 16th

phrases.english: but does not replant it in a dry place.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר מוּתָּר בַּעֲשִׂיַּית מְלָאכָה? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה's view as just established.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view that Judea may work on the 14th until midday
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא sets the replanting case on the 13th. This implies that on the 14th such work is forbidden, which contradicts רבי יהודה allowing work in Judea.

steps.title: Why does רבי יהודה say the 13th and not the 14th?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from רבי יהודה's ruling that replanting is allowed on the 13th but not the 14th. Since a plant takes root in three days, the 14th would also have worked if work were allowed then.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the 13th, yes; on the 14th, no. After all, we heard רבי יהודה say that any graft that does not take hold within three days will not take hold anymore. If you think the 14th is permitted for work, why did he need to say the 13th? There is still the 14th, the 15th, and part of the 16th!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge from step 13. רבי יהודה said 'the 13th,' so the 14th must be forbidden, even though the 14th would still give the plant three days to take root before the עומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stalk that takes root before the עומר on the 16th becomes permitted by the עומר, and רבי יהודה holds that rooting takes three days. Replanting on the 14th would still leave three days: the 14th, the 15th, and part of the 16th. Since he mentioned only the 13th, the 14th must be forbidden for work, which contradicts the idea that he permits work on the 14th in יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: After all / now, since (introduces a known fact used in an argument)
And if it would enter your mind (introduces an assumption that will be shown wrong)
But there is! (points out something that was ignored)

steps.confusionAlert: The 16th matters because the עומר is brought then, and the עומר permits new grain that rooted before it. That is why the count of days ends at the 16th.

phrases.english: On the thirteenth, yes,
phrases.notes: Inference from the wording of רבי יהודה's ruling.

phrases.english: on the fourteenth, no.

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדִי שָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה דְּאָמַר:
phrases.english: After all, we heard רבי יהודה say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַרְכָּבָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ קוֹלֶטֶת לִשְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים —
phrases.english: Any graft that does not take hold within three days,
will no longer take hold.
phrases.notes: So three days is the rooting time.

phrases.english: And if it would enter your mind
that the fourteenth is permitted for doing work,
why do I need the thirteenth?
But there is the fourteenth, the fifteenth, and part of the sixteenth!
phrases.notes: Three days before the עומר, counting part of the 16th.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 13 by spelling out the inference and the three-day calculation.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view in the ברייתא of step 11 that רבי יהודה permits work on the 14th in יהודה until midday.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the 14th were permitted, replanting then would still allow three days of rooting before the עומר. So רבי יהודה should have said the 14th, and his choice of the 13th implies the 14th is forbidden.

steps.title: רבא: the ruling is about the גליל
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that רבי יהודה's ruling refers to the גליל, where no work is done on the 14th at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: They taught this about the גליל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. The replanting ruling was said about the גליל, where even רבי יהודה agrees that work is forbidden on the 14th.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא of step 11, רבי יהודה said the גליל did no work on ערב פסח. So in the גליל the 14th is not an option, and the 13th is the last day to replant. This says nothing against רבי יהודה permitting work in יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught (refers to a teaching of the תנאים)

phrases.english: Rava said:
They taught it about the Galilee.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the location of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the replanting ruling applied in יהודה, where the 14th is permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling is about the גליל, where the 14th is forbidden, so the 13th is the last day.

steps.title: But what about the night before the 14th?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks that even in the גליל, work is allowed on the night of the 14th according to בית הלל, so that night could have been mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the night!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's answer. Even in the גליל, the night before the 14th is permitted for work according to בית הלל, so רבי יהודה could have taught the case for that night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה (step 8) recorded that בית שמאי forbid work on the night of the 14th, while בית הלל permit it until sunrise. If the night is permitted, replanting then would be a bigger חידוש than the 13th. So why did רבי יהודה say the 13th?

keyTerms.meaning: The night (here, the night before the 14th)

phrases.english: But there is the night!
phrases.notes: The night between the 13th and the 14th.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's answer that the ruling is about the גליל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to בית הלל, the night of the 14th is permitted even in the גליל. So רבי יהודה should have mentioned that night instead of the 13th.

steps.title: רב ששת: רבי יהודה follows בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that this ruling follows בית שמאי, who forbid work even on the night of the 14th.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: It follows בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question about the night. The ruling follows בית שמאי, for whom the night is also forbidden, so the 13th is truly the last time to replant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית שמאי, the night of the 14th is already forbidden in the גליל. That leaves the 13th as the last possible day. The cost of this answer is that it ties רבי יהודה to בית שמאי, whose view is not the accepted הלכה.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
It follows Beit Shammai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the ruling to a specific opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the ruling follows בית הלל, who permit work at night.
steps.terutzMaskana: It follows בית שמאי, who forbid work at night, so the 13th is the last day.

steps.title: רב אשי: people do not weed at night
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the ruling can follow בית הלל. The night was not mentioned because people do not normally weed at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Really it follows בית הלל. He did not mention the night because people do not usually weed at night.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives another answer to the question about the night. He keeps רבי יהודה in line with בית הלל and explains that the night was not mentioned because people do not weed in the dark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Work at night may be allowed, but רבי יהודה was describing a normal real-life case. Since nobody weeds in the dark, the last realistic time to accidentally uproot a stalk is the 13th. This avoids linking רבי יהודה to בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (keeps the original assumption and explains it differently)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Really, it follows Beit Hillel,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין דַּרְכָּן שֶׁל בְּנֵי אָדָם
phrases.english: because it is not the way of people
to weed at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם כְּבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the challenge of step 16, disagreeing with רב ששת's approach.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reality: the case describes typical behavior
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the night is permitted, רבי יהודה should have mentioned it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The night is permitted, but people do not weed at night, so it was not a realistic case to mention.

steps.title: רבינא: in יהודה, only one partial day counts for rooting
steps.stepSummary: רבינא keeps the ruling in יהודה. For a plant taking root, only one partial day can count as a full day, and replanting on the 14th would need two partial days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Really it is about יהודה. For taking root, we apply 'part of the day is like the whole day' once, but we do not apply it twice.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a completely different answer to the original challenge of step 14. The ruling can be about יהודה, where the 14th is permitted, because replanting on the 14th would not give the plant enough real time to root.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Replanting on the 13th gives part of the 13th, all of the 14th, and all of the 15th, so only one partial day is counted. Replanting on the 14th would need part of the 14th and part of the 16th, which is two partial days. That is too little real time for a plant to root, so the 13th is the last day even though work is permitted on the 14th in יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Part of the day counts like the whole day

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain why רבי יהודה said the 13th. רבא says the ruling is about the גליל, where the 14th is forbidden. רבינא says it is about יהודה, and replanting on the 14th fails because it would require counting two partial days. On רבינא's view, רבי יהודה still permits work on the 14th in יהודה.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבינא's answer keeps רבי יהודה's view from the ברייתא in step 11, that work is permitted on the 14th in יהודה, without moving the case to the גליל.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Really, it is about Judea,
and regarding taking root, one 'part of the day is like all of it' we do say,
phrases.notes: Part of the 13th counts as a full day.

phrases.english: two 'part of the day is like all of it' we do not say.
phrases.notes: Part of the 14th and part of the 16th cannot both count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the challenge of step 14 and offers an alternative to רבא's answer in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the calculation behind the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Replanting on the 14th would still give three days: the 14th, the 15th, and part of the 16th.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only one partial day can count toward rooting. The 14th would need two partial days, so the 13th is the last day even in יהודה.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: work begun before the 14th may be finished on it
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. רבי מאיר rules that work started before the 14th may be finished on the 14th, but new work may not be started on the 14th.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי מאיר says: Any work a person started before the 14th, he may finish on the 14th. But he may not start it fresh on the 14th, even if he can finish it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new משנה. רבי מאיר gives a rule for work on ערב פסח: you may finish what you started, but you may not begin something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding factor is when the work was started, not how long it takes. Even a short job that could be finished before חצות may not be started on the 14th. Work already in progress, however, may be completed.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)

phrases.english: MISHNA: Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מְלָאכָה שֶׁהִתְחִיל בָּהּ קוֹדֶם לְאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר,
phrases.english: Any work that one began before the fourteenth,
he may finish it on the fourteenth.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא יַתְחִיל בָּהּ בַּתְּחִלָּה בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר,
phrases.english: But he may not begin it fresh on the fourteenth,
even though he is able to finish it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Work begun before the 14th may be completed on the 14th, but new work may not be started on the 14th.

steps.title: חכמים: only three crafts may work until חצות
steps.stepSummary: חכמים say that only tailors, barbers, and launderers may work on ערב פסח, and only until חצות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חכמים say: Three crafts may work on ערב פסח until חצות. They are: tailors, barbers, and launderers.
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים give a different view from רבי מאיר. Instead of asking whether the work was started earlier, they allow only three specific crafts to work until חצות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חכמים, what matters is the type of work, not when it began. These three crafts produce things people need for the יום טוב: clothing, haircuts, and clean garments. All other work is forbidden on the 14th, even if it was started earlier.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
three crafts may do work
on Passover eve until midday,
and these are they:
the tailors, the barbers, and the launderers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי מאיר within the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only tailors, barbers, and launderers may work on ערב פסח, and only until חצות.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בר יהודה adds shoemakers
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר יהודה adds shoemakers to the list of crafts permitted on ערב פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: Shoemakers too.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר יהודה accepts the approach of חכמים but adds a fourth craft, shoemakers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees that certain crafts are permitted because people need them for the יום טוב. He holds that shoes, which people need for the רגל, belong on that list too.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:
Shoemakers too.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף רַצְעָנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth craft to the list given by חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shoemakers may also work on ערב פסח until חצות.

steps.title: Which kind of work does רבי מאיר's rule cover?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי מאיר's rule (finish yes, start no) refers to work לצורך המועד, to work שלא לצורך המועד, or to both.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A question was asked. Did we learn רבי מאיר's rule about work that is for the festival? Then work that is not for the festival may not even be finished. Or maybe we learned it about work that is not for the festival? Then work that is for the festival may even be started. Or maybe, for both kinds, finishing is allowed and starting is not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking what kind of work רבי מאיר was talking about in the משנה. It offers three possible readings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option 1: the rule is about work לצורך המועד, so work that is not for the festival is forbidden completely. Option 2: the rule is about work שלא לצורך המועד, so festival work is fully allowed, even starting it. Option 3: the rule applies to both kinds the same way, finishing yes and starting no.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them (a real open question)
For the needs of the festival

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two variables. One is the type of work (for the festival or not). The other is the stage of the work (finishing or starting). The three options are different ways of combining them.

phrases.english: GEMARA: A question was asked before them:
Was it about work for the festival's needs that we learned (the rule),
but work not for the festival's needs —
may not even be finished?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא: שֶׁלֹּא לְצוֹרֶךְ הַמּוֹעֵד תְּנַן,
phrases.english: Or perhaps we learned it about work not for the festival's needs,
but work for its needs — we may even start it?
Or perhaps, both work for the festival's needs
and work not for its needs:
finishing — yes; starting — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of רבי מאיר's ruling in the new משנה (Step 20).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי מאיר's 'finish but don't start' rule is limited to festival work, limited to non-festival work, or applies to both.

steps.title: Proof from the small belt and small hairnet
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says one may not start even a small belt or hairnet on the 14th. The word 'even' seems to show these are festival items, so non-festival work may not even be finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'But one may not start new work on the 14th, even a small belt, even a small hairnet.' What does 'even' mean? Doesn't it mean that even these, which are for the festival, may be finished but not started? That would show that work not for the festival may not even be finished!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to answer the question. It reads the word 'even' as pointing to festival items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works like this. If even festival items like a belt or hairnet can only be finished and not started, then non-festival work must be stricter and may not even be finished. That supports Option 1.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference, from this it follows

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא יַתְחִיל בַּתְּחִילָּה בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר
phrases.english: But one may not begin from the outset on the fourteenth
even a small belt,
even a small hairnet.
What does 'even' mean?
Is it not: even these, which are for the festival's needs,
finishing — yes, starting — no?!
It follows that work not for its needs —
we may not even finish!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אֲבָל לֹא יַתְחִיל בַּתְּחִילָּה בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of Step 23 in favor of Option 1.
steps.raayaObject: Option 1: the rule refers to festival work, and non-festival work may not even be finished.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא forbidding starting even a small belt or hairnet on the 14th, with 'even' read as 'even festival items.'

steps.title: 'Even' means even small items
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. 'Even' may mean 'even small items.' One might think that since they are finished as soon as they are started, starting them is allowed. The ברייתא teaches that it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really, even work not for the festival may be finished. And what does 'even' mean? Even these, which are small. You might have thought that since starting them is the same as finishing them, we may start them from the outset. The ברייתא teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof by giving a different meaning to the word 'even.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Even' is not about festival versus non-festival. It is about size. Small items are finished almost right away, so one might think starting them is really just finishing. The ברייתא teaches that starting is still forbidden. So the ברייתא fits Option 3 too, and the גמרא tries another proof in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth (introduces the pushed-off reading)
You might have thought to say

phrases.english: No, really, work not for its needs
we may also finish,
and what does 'even' mean?
Even these too, which are small,
for it could enter your mind to say:
their beginning is the completion of their work —
so let us also start them from the outset;
it teaches us (that we may not).

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְעוֹלָם דְּשֶׁלֹּא לְצוֹרֶךְ מִיגְמַר נָמֵי גָּמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 24 by reading 'even' differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. The question of Step 23 remains unresolved.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'even' means 'even festival items.' It can just as easily mean 'even small items, which are finished as soon as they are started.'
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא of the small belt and hairnet does not settle the question. 'Even' can refer to small size, not to festival need.

steps.title: A second proof from רבי מאיר himself begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new proof, quoting רבי מאיר about any work that is לצורך המועד. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי מאיר says: Any work that is for the needs of the festival —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next attempt to answer the question. It starts quoting a statement of רבי מאיר, and the rest comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since this source is רבי מאיר's own words and speaks directly about work לצורך המועד, it may clarify which option he holds. The actual proof is completed in the continuation.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rabbi Meir says:
Any work that is for the needs of the festival —

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע. רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: כׇּל מְלָאכָה שֶׁהִיא לְצוֹרֶךְ הַמּוֹעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected (Step 25), the גמרא begins a second proof for the question of Step 23.
steps.raayaObject: Clarifying which reading of רבי מאיר's rule is correct (to be completed on the next amud).
steps.raayaSupportSource: A statement of רבי מאיר about any work that is for the needs of the festival.
